fall_height_m.notes: No peer-reviewed estimate exists as of September 2026. Public figures read in this session: 1,200 m (Kathmandu Post, 28 Aug 2026, reporting Planet Labs imagery analysis: 'falling 1,200 metres into the valley') and 1,000 m (Mohd. Farooq Azam, ICIMOD, quoted by the Kathmandu Post: 'hit the valley 1000 meters below'). A 2,100 m figure also circulates publicly but no retrievable source stating it was found, so the range is not recorded as a disputed Range.

rock_fraction.notes: USGS: 'it is unclear if the initial slope failure was a landslide incorporating part of a glacier or a glacial collapse'; no fraction has been published.

seismic.agency_range.notes: Only the USGS ComCat magnitude (5.2 ms_vx) was read; the initial 4.4 was a preliminary USGS value, not another agency.

source_volume_m3.notes: No peer-reviewed estimate exists as of September 2026. The only figure read in this session is the range quoted from Mohd. Farooq Azam (ICIMOD) by the Kathmandu Post on 28 Aug 2026: 'The glacier collapse was 100 to 200 million cubic meters in size'. ICIMOD's own press release speaks only of 'a large volume of ice and rock debris'; USGS gives no volume.

infrastructure_impacts.description: USGS: the debris flow and flood 'impacted populated areas downstream along the Lende Kholā and Trishuli̇̄ Kholā rivers, including the Rasuwāgaḍhi̇̄ border post'; 'a vital highway connecting China and Nepal' likely buried or destroyed
Kathmandu Post (30 Aug 2026) quoting the Nepal Electricity Authority spokesperson: 'The Rasuwagadhi Hydropower Project has been completely washed away'
Kathmandu Post (30 Aug 2026) quoting the NEA: 'the Chilime project has been buried'; Kathmandu Post (26 Aug 2026): a resident reported the Chilime project damaged
Kathmandu Post (30 Aug 2026): among 'at least 13 hydropower projects ... damaged in Rasuwa and Nuwakot districts' the affected operational projects include '60MW Upper Trishuli A'

Kathmandu Post (26 Aug 2026): 'A sudden surge in the Bhotekoshi river has damaged settlements and infrastructure in Timure and Syabrubesi'; the Timure helipad was swept away. Kathmandu Post (31 Aug 2026): the Gosaikunda rural municipality building in Timure was 'swept away'
Kathmandu Post (26 Aug 2026): settlements and infrastructure in Timure and Syabrubesi damaged; the Syabrubesi hydrological station gauge was swept away (Kathmandu Post, 2 Sep 2026)

name: Langtang Lirung / Lhende Khola / Bhote Koshi / Trishuli rock–ice avalanche cascade, Nepal–Tibet
notes: Target event. Figures from USGS ComCat and the USGS event page are agency values; everything else is press (Kathmandu Post) or ICIMOD and carries no best. failure_type follows the Kathmandu Post quoting Azam (ICIMOD): 'the flood was triggered by a bedrock failure. When the bedrock gave way, the glacier on top also got swept', while USGS states the mechanism is unclear. dammed_river / secondary_surge are true on the Kathmandu Post's account (debris blocked the Lhende Khola, a temporary lake formed and the blockage failed; ICIMOD said it was investigating a landslide dam) — press-reported, not yet peer-reviewed. Transect ids are those of the lhende-khola-trishuli AOI; the public arrival figures of ~7.5 min (Rasuwagadhi) and ~45 min (Betrawati) are recorded only as unattributed public figures in the transect descriptions. Fatalities cover Nepal only; Chinese casualties were not read from a citable source.

magnitude.notes: ComCat preferred magnitude 4.2 ms_vx (magnitude-error 0.148), event type landslide, reviewed

related_seismic.notes: Second signal at 06:00:35 UTC, 'about three hours after' the first (ComCat; USGS event page). ComCat: 'identified during post-processing of low-frequency seismic records ... Due to the lack of high-frequency energy, a precise location could not be determined, so we fixed this event's location to that of the initial landslide.' agency_range not read.

runout_km.notes: USGS: 'The debris flow and flood travelled approximately 100 kilometers (approximately 62 miles)'; 'nearly 100 km' elsewhere on the page. Preliminary

magnitude.notes: ComCat preferred magnitude 5.2 ms_vx (magnitude-error 0.09), event type landslide, reviewed

seismic.notes: ComCat general text: initially reported as a magnitude 4.4 earthquake; 'Additional analysis of nearby seismic stations, long period seismic waves, and satellite imagery led to the determination that the seismic event was instead a glacial collapse and debris flow, and that no earthquake had occurred.' No single-force inversion was read, so single_force stays false.

source_elevation_m.notes: Kathmandu Post (28 Aug 2026), reporting Planet Labs imagery analysis: 'a large section — about 600 metres (2,000 feet) wide — of glacier and rock had collapsed from an altitude of 5,200 metres'. Press-only, no best

time.basis: usgs_comcat_origin of us7000tbwb (event type landslide, reviewed); the Kathmandu Post gives the same instant as 08:37 local time

transect_observations.description: USGS: the Rasuwagadhi border post was impacted; Kathmandu Post (27 Aug 2026): 'The Bhotekoshi rose with extraordinary speed at the Rasuwagadhi border crossing on Wednesday morning'. An arrival time of about 7.5 minutes after the ComCat origin circulates publicly without attribution; no retrieved source states it, so arrival_time_min is null.

arrival_time_min.notes: Kathmandu Post (2 Sep 2026): 'the glacier collapsed at 8:37 AM on August 26' and 'at 8:50 AM, the flash flood swept away the gauge in the Bhotekoshi river in Rasuwa, at the Syabrubesi hydrological station' — the 13 minutes are the difference of the two stated clock times (Nepal time); press-only, no best

transect_observations.description: Gauge of the DHM Syabrubesi hydrological station destroyed at 08:50 local time; no stage figure was read. A public figure of 13–14 minutes is consistent with the stated clock times.

Kathmandu Post (27 Aug 2026): 'Bridges and other infrastructure between Rasuwa and Dhading were swept away'. An arrival time of about 45 minutes after the origin circulates publicly without attribution; no retrieved source states it, so arrival_time_min is null.

Stage rise of up to 9 m within 30 minutes at the DHM Galchhi station (ICIMOD; Kathmandu Post); Malekhu downstream rose about 7 m over a similar period. The arrival clock time at Galchhi was not read, so arrival_time_min is null.

stage_rise_m.notes: ICIMOD press release (26 Aug 2026, citing DHM): 'Water levels on the Trishuli River at Galchchi reportedly rose by as much as nine metres within 30 minutes'; Kathmandu Post (27 Aug 2026): 'At Galchhi, the Trishuli river rose by as much as nine metres in just 30 minutes ... according to ICIMOD'. 'As much as' and 'reportedly', so no best
